source_text:
Scholia in Apocalypsem (scholia 1, 3-39)
̓Επεὶ δὲ ἀνακειμένῳ μοι τῷ λόγῳ, τῆς φήμης διατρεχούσης περὶ τῆς ἕξεως ἡμῶν,
προσῄεσαν ὁτὲ μὲν αἱρετικοί, ὁτὲ δὲ οἱ ἀπὸ τῶν Ἑλληνικῶν μαθημάτων καὶ μάλιστα
τῶν ἐν φιλοσοφίᾳ, ἔδοξεν ἐξετάσαι τά τε τῶν αἱρετικῶν δόγματα καὶ τὰ ὑπὸ τῶν
thought_title: Why Origen examined heretics and philosophers
orientation: Origen is narrating in the first person how, as his reputation spread, both heretics and people trained in Greek learning came to him, which led him to decide to examine their teachings.
pass_a_gloss: But since, while I was devoted to the word, the report spreading concerning our condition, there came to me sometimes heretics, sometimes those from Greek learning and especially those in philosophy, it seemed good to examine both the doctrines of the heretics and the things by the

choices.english: while I was devoted to the word
choices.why: The dative participle with μοι expresses Origen's ongoing state of dedication to the word or teaching; 'devoted' captures the sense of being set upon or given to it.
rejected: while I was reclining at the word
when I was at leisure for the word

choices.term: τῆς φήμης διατρεχούσης περὶ τῆς ἕξεως ἡμῶν
choices.english: the report running about concerning our condition
choices.why: The genitive absolute is rendered as a circumstantial clause; 'running about' keeps the motion of διατρεχούσης, and 'condition' renders ἕξεως as the state or disposition being reported.
rejected: the fame spreading about our habit
the rumor going around about our possession

choices.why: The imperfect of πρόσειμι indicates repeated or ongoing approach; 'there came to me' preserves the iterative force and the dative μοι.
The correlative pair marks alternating groups; 'sometimes' keeps the distributive sense without over-translating.
rejected: at one time ... at another time

choices.why: The prepositional phrase with ἀπό indicates origin or background; 'those from the Greek learning' is literal and preserves the source's construction.
The impersonal aorist ἔδοξεν with infinitive expresses a decision; 'it seemed good' is the standard literal rendering and keeps the impersonal construction.
